text:
Maya: Quick question — trying to reconcile routing/quota semantics when we expose the same internal endpoints over gRPC and HTTP JSON via the edge gateway. How should we annotate requests so the console can attribute cost/latency per model+route? e.g.

Maya: Proposed headers: `x-rw-route`, `x-rw-client`, `x-rw-variant` and keep `x-request-id` for trace. Gateway can translate protobuf method -> route name.

Liam: +1 to headers, but browser SDK can't set arbitrary headers for simple fetch. We should support a query param fallback for web (~?route=...). Also CORS implications.

Sanjay: Observability wise, prefer canonical route label in trace/span name and as Prometheus label. Example prom query: `sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="redwood.generate.v1"}[5m])) by (quantile)` — otherwise console charts will be noisy.

Zoe: Also think about quota scoping. gRPC unary vs streaming has different costing (tokens vs active-stream-hours). We need a mapping table in control plane so the quota service can map method+content-type -> billing metric.

Maya: Good point. Maybe a small translation layer in control-plane: proto method -> canonicalRoute + costingScheme. This layer can be hot-reloaded for rollouts.

Liam: For rollouts UX: console should show "translation layer version" and diffs when you change mapping. Helps debug sudden quota changes.

Sanjay: Agree. Also add a "sampling" flag in headers so we can turn on payload sampling for a subset of traffic (PII safe toggle). `x-rw-sample=1` :eyes: 

deploy-bot: deploy started for controlplane/route-translator v2 -> prod

Maya: I'll sketch an RFC and add a small PoC that translates grpc method -> route + header fallback + prometheus labels. Anyone want in on the PoC? :coffee:

Liam: I'll pair on the CORS/query param piece.

Zoe: I'll mock the quota mapping table and a couple example costing rules.

Sanjay: I'll wire up the Prometheus labels and a sample Grafana panel.

Maya: sweet. Thanks everyone.
